A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same R2F/R2F+ work. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, including the retained Appendices A–J and newly added K–P in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments on RareBench, DVMP and T2I-CompBench, with automatic and human evaluations, ablations and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds IterComp results, accelerated FLUX experiments, guidance diagnostics, image-quality measurements and GPU profiling.

M1.justification: The standard R2F and R2F+ procedures remain unchanged. Appendix K introduces a four-step FLUX-schnell adaptation that replaces alternating guidance with text-embedding blending during selected early steps, followed by rare-prompt-only sampling. This adapts an existing ablation component into an accelerated variant.

E1.justification: Evaluation coverage remains RareBench, DVMP and T2I-CompBench. New experiments use retained tasks and subsets; LAION-400M, already used for frequency analysis in Figure 2, supplies mapping information in Appendix M. Speech, music and foundation-model applications are proposed without experiments.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds IterComp as an evaluated comparator alongside R2F using IterComp. The original nine main baselines remain, and FLUX was already evaluated in v1; its new four-step comparison does not introduce a previously absent baseline.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark protocols are retained, but v2 substantially extends evaluation procedures: four-step FLUX inference, late frequent-prompt exposure, corpus-frequency mapping controls, and three image-quality metrics—LAION-aesthetic, PickScore and ImageReward. Appendix O also introduces diffusion-time and peak-memory profiling on a specified two-object prompt.

E4.justification: Appendices L–O add substantive analyses of whether late frequent prompts displace the target concept, whether LAION frequencies improve mappings, whether R2F+ compromises image quality, and its computational overhead. These complement retained ablations and failure cases; Table 4 also extends backbone robustness evidence to IterComp.

E5.justification: Table 17 newly reports image-quality scores with ± values, but does not define the uncertainty measure or its estimation procedure. The existing seed-42 setting and eight-seed visualizations remain unchanged. No increase in repeated runs or explicit significance test is documented.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores are retained, while Table 4 and Tables 15–18 add substantial results. Within the new four-step comparison, FLUX/R2F-FLUX property scores are 72.5/78.7, but complex scores are 73.7/68.7. LAION mapping variants score below standard R2F, and newly reported diffusion times are 20.60 seconds for R2F versus 72.37 for R2F+.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1, its assumptions and the complete Appendix A proof are unchanged. Appendix O adds a simple, empirically motivated runtime derivation for R2F+: N(T+1)+(T+10), combining per-object generation and masking with final guided generation.

C1.justification: The central claims remain training-free frequent-concept guidance, flexibility across diffusion models and LLMs, the R2F+ extension, RareBench, and alignment improvements up to 28.1 percentage points. Adding IterComp to the introduction's comparison list supports the retained superiority claim without redefining the central contributions.

C2.justification: New interpretations explain frequent-concept drift through late-step conditioning and weaker LAION mappings through caption quality and training-distribution mismatch. Additional discussion addresses short-step applicability, R2F+ quality and computational tradeoffs, and potential cross-modal applications. Existing overlapping-box failure limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix K specifies blending settings and scheduling, Appendix M documents frequency extraction and top-20-word prompting, and Appendix O identifies a 40GB A100 and the scope of timing measurements. The code link changes from Rare2Frequent to Rare-to-Frequent; availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting image-quality assessment and prospective applications, including ImageReward, SpatialVLM, visual instruction tuning and speech/audio/music generation. Section 2 and the central positioning against existing compositional and LLM-grounded diffusion approaches remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites explain acceleration, IterComp comparisons and new appendix references, and the header becomes 'Preprint, Under review.' Appendices K–P extend the document without substantially reorganizing the existing narrative or Appendices A–J.

P2.justification: v2 expands Table 4, adds Tables 15–18 and Figures 16–17, reformats Table 13, and resizes several illustrations. Figure 10 relabels the unchanged imagery from 'star-shaped panda' to 'star-shaped spaceship.' The established visual organization is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens practical validation through additional backbone and acceleration tests, mapping and guidance diagnostics, and quantitative R2F+ quality/cost evidence. These address limited gaps in an already extensive evaluation. Undefined ± statistics and an optimistic acceleration interpretation despite the complex-category decline limit the gains, but the added evidence and computational transparency provide a clear net improvement.
